subject: Post-call: model-fit recommendations + acceptance checklist for Acme Payments
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@acmepay.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmepay.com
Date: 2027-05-28T15:30:00Z
Subject: Thanks — sample data + a few clarifying points

Vivek,

Thanks for the call earlier — good overview. As discussed, I attached a small representative sample of our production requests (30k rows, redacted). Key asks / concerns from our side: 

- We need parity (or very close) vs our internal proprietary baseline on three critical intents: payment routing, dispute triage, and refund eligibility. The baseline is a custom 12B model tuned on our transcripts.
- Latency budget: median inference < 150ms for single-request sync flows.
- Token cost sensitivity: we run ~10M calls/month; anything that materially increases per-token spend is a blocker.
- Risk: we cannot accept frequent quality regressions after rollouts; need a clear acceptance checklist and regression detection cadence.

Could you send recommended open-model candidates to trial, the minimal prompt set we should evaluate, and a suggested acceptance threshold matrix? Also please include any existing benchmark runs that are comparable.

I tried to attach the sample but the email client truncated size — I’ve uploaded the zip to our S3 and share the link separately if needed. Looking to move fast — is a 30-minute follow-up on Monday possible?

—Samir
Product Lead, Acme Payments

Attachments: acme_prod_sample.zip (csv)

Subject: Re: Thanks — sample data + a few clarifying points

Samir — thanks for the clear list and for the sample. Quick recap + what we’ll do next: 

Recap from our side:
- Primary goal: match your proprietary baseline on the three intents while keeping median latency < 150ms for sync flows.
- Constraints: strict cost sensitivity and low regression tolerance.

Immediate next steps (what Redwood will run):
1) Run a parity evaluation against a set of curated open models and our smaller distilled variants on your sample set. Initial candidates we recommend for trial:
   - OpenLambda-34B-chat (8-bit quantized) — balanced quality/cost for dialog-style prompts
   - Falcon-40B-instruct-quant — strong instruction-following, good on structured outputs
   - Redwood-Edge-12B (distilled internal variant) — optimized for latency and token cost (we’ll surface exact perf profile)
2) Use your sample + a 120-case prompt set (attached prompt_set_v1.txt) to calculate: top-intent F1, routing precision/recall, and a refund-eligibility binary accuracy.
3) Deliver: benchmark report (metrics + latency distribution), a minimal acceptance checklist, and recommended rollout plan (canary sizes, rollback criteria).

Timing: I’ll get the first evaluation results by Monday EOD PT if we can pull the sample from your S3. Can you share the link or grant the redwood-evals role read access?

I’ve attached the prompt set we’ll run first and a short SOW draft for quick procurement review.

Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | redwood.ai

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-29T09:12:00Z
Subject: INTERNAL: proposed acceptance thresholds + eval plan for Acme (notes)

Vivek / team — internal note before we send the formal checklist. I ran a quick scan of similar accounts and recommend the following acceptance thresholds for initial parity (these are intentionally conservative so we don’t oversell):

Metric thresholds (initial gate):
- Top-intent F1 >= 0.88 (baseline reported at ~0.90)
- Routing precision >= 0.86 and recall >= 0.84
- Refund-eligibility binary accuracy >= 0.90 (baseline ~0.92)
- Median latency for 1r/s sync <= 150ms (95th <= 350ms on dedicated pool)
- Failure rate (timeouts/errors) <= 0.5%

Regression detection cadence / policy:
- Run daily smoke evals on a 3k-sample from production traffic for the first 30 days after rollout.
- Alert if any metric drops > 2.5% absolute vs canary baseline or below acceptance gate.
- Automatic rollback if any critical metric drops >5% or if daily failure rate > 1% for 3 consecutive days.

Recommended evaluation artifacts to share with Acme:
- Full CSV of per-row predictions + confidence scores (deliverable)
- Prompt set used (prompt_set_v1.txt) — keep canonical copy in drive link and commit to their repo for reproducibility
- Jupyter notebook with error analysis and examples where model disagreed with baseline (we should flag types of regressions: hallucination on refund rules, missed routing triggers)

Ask: Vivek — can you confirm the perf targets (latency/cost) are measurable in the hosted canary and on their committed dedicated pool? If yes we’ll include the rollout sizing in the SOW.

Marissa Cole
Principal ML Solutions, Redwood Inference
